feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: Here's how to watch election night as the polls close, hour-by-hour
entry.summary: As polls close on election night, here's a look at what to expect each hour and which midterm races are key to deciding control of Congress.

entry.title: Supreme Court hears religious freedom case centered on universal pre-K program
entry.summary: The Archdiocese of Denver wants to be able to turn away LGBTQ families from Catholic preschools that receive state funding.

entry.title: How one family gave a critical boost to gene therapy research
entry.summary: A family affected by Sanfilippo syndrome raised millions of dollars for research. The Food and Drug Administration just approved a gene therapy the support helped make possible.

entry.title: Trump thanks supporters for the memories in final campaign stops for 2026 midterms
entry.summary: President Trump has maintained a near-daily rally schedule as Election Day draws closer, playing his greatest hits for loyal crowds in red states in what is a sort-of goodbye to campaigning.

entry.title: What's it like to run for Congress when the odds are stacked heavily against you?
entry.summary: The majority of congressional races this cycle are rated either solid Democrat or solid Republican. They're the opposite of tossups, where candidates from the minority party face near impossible odds.

entry.title: The National Symphony Orchestra is at a crossroads. Can it survive?
entry.summary: When the Kennedy Center closed in September, it left an important American orchestra without a home. The players, and their charismatic conductor, have taken their show out onto an uncertain road.

entry.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
entry.summary: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

entry.title: Virginia and D.C. sue to block construction of Trump arch
entry.summary: U.S. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkin ordered both sides to talk and to agree on a proposed briefing schedule on the motion for a temporary restraining order by Saturday evening.

entry.title: France seethes again as youth-led protests sweep Europe
entry.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk" of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween, as some 320,000 people nationwide took to the streets.

entry.title: Key takeaways from this week's political meeting in Beijing
entry.summary: The Communist party central committee meeting was focused on discipline and fighting corruption. It comes ahead of next year when Xi is widely expected to try to secure a fourth term.
